# R4 Gal 4:8–31 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** 4050–4501
**Lines actually read:** 4050–4498 (body through additional notes and section outline; range ends at structural outline L4490–4498)
**Claim count:** 42

## Claims

### C-R4-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo places the fundamental move from argument (3:7–4:7) to appeal at 4:8, though some locate the shift at 4:12 (forensic to deliberative rhetoric); he allows 4:8–11 is transitional but holds exhortatory tone begins in v. 8.
- **quote:** "we think the tone of exhortation begins in verse 8."
- **locus:** L4052
- **passage:** Gal 4:8–31

### C-R4-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** The appeal has three sections: past of the Galatians (4:8–11), past of Paul and the Galatians (4:12–20), and present status via Scripture urging resistance to the agitators (4:21–31).
- **quote:** "Paul’s appeal falls into three distinct sections."
- **locus:** L4054
- **passage:** Gal 4:8–31

### C-R4-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, stoicheia, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Unit 4:8–11 centers on consternation that the Galatians are abandoning gospel freedom for renewed slavery under the “elements of the world”; it applies the wider argument of 3:7–4:7, not only 4:1–7.
- **quote:** "4:8–11 applies the wider argument of which 4:1–7 is the conclusion"
- **locus:** L4062
- **passage:** Gal 4:8–11

### C-R4-004
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 4:8 Paul portrays the Galatians’ former state as not knowing God and being enslaved to beings who by nature are not gods; “not knowing God” especially describes Gentile non-Christians with OT-style relational knowledge.
- **quote:** "\"Not knowing God\" is a way of describing non-Christians and especially Gentile non-Christians"
- **locus:** L4068
- **passage:** Gal 4:8

### C-R4-005
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo prefers that the false “gods” exist but are not truly gods (demonic), citing 1 Cor 10:19–20, rather than that they simply do not exist.
- **quote:** "The latter is probably to be preferred; see especially Paul’s claim in 1 Cor. 10:19–20"
- **locus:** L4068
- **passage:** Gal 4:8

### C-R4-006
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In 4:9 Paul uses a once/but now contrast and “corrects” “having come to know God” with “having come to be known by God,” stressing divine initiative and election-like knowledge so as to highlight grace.
- **quote:** "Humans do indeed come to know God, but they do so only because God first determines to \"know\" us in Christ."
- **locus:** L4070
- **passage:** Gal 4:9

### C-R4-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** For the Galatians, adding law adherence would “complete” their relationship with God (cf. 3:3); for Paul such addition is subtraction, questioning the adequacy of God’s provision in Christ.
- **quote:** "such a step of addition is in fact subtraction, implicitly calling into question the adequacy of God’s provision in Christ."
- **locus:** L4072
- **passage:** Gal 4:9

### C-R4-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, stoicheia, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** The “elements” of 4:9 are the same as 4:3’s “elements of the world”; Moo renders πτωχά as “impotent” (lacking spiritual worth) rather than merely “miserable.”

- **locus:** L4074

### C-R4-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, stoicheia, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Stoicheia are the basic material building blocks of the universe often tied to idolatrous worship, so referring to pre-Christian religions; for the warning to work, law must be a subset of the elements—equating advance into Judaism with regression into heathenism, without fully “demonizing” the law.
- **quote:** "he implies that putting themselves under the law, since the era of the law has ended with the coming of the promised Seed, is akin to returning to their impotent pagan religions."
- **locus:** L4074
- **passage:** Gal 4:9

### C-R4-010
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, stoicheia, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** The observances of 4:10 (days, months, seasons, years) are governed by heavenly bodies and thus identify with the stoicheia of v. 9 better than equating elements with the non-gods of v. 8.

### C-R4-011

- **claim:** “Days” likely Sabbath and festival days; “months” new moons; “seasons” multi-day festivals; “years” sabbatical years—yet Paul deliberately avoids technical Jewish terms (contrast Col 2:16) to tie observances to the elements and perhaps pagan past.

## Coverage summary

**4:8–11 (L4050–4080):** Structural placement of Appeal; former Gentile slavery to non-gods; once/now knowing / known by God; return to weak/impotent stoicheia as law under elements; calendrical observances tied to heavenly bodies; fear of labor in vain.

**4:12–20 (L4086–4174):** Pathos personal appeal; become like Paul (law-free); first visit illness (physical, likely eyes); no despising; received as angel/Christ; lost blessing; enemy by gospel-truth; agitators’ bad zeal/exclusion; good to be courted well; birth pains until Christ formed; wish to change voice; perplexity. Textual notes on 4:14, 18, 19 and Calvin on voice change noted but not claimed as Moo’s main exegesis.

**4:21–31 (L4180–4484):** Mixed argument/appeal; defensive Hagar–Sarah use; slave/free leitmotif; allegory method (figurative, historical + typology-tempered); two covenants (Sinai/Hagar vs. likely Abrahamic/Christ); Arabia clause syntax; present Jerusalem = contemporary law-focused Judaism (not only agitators); Jerusalem above free mother; Isa 54:1 as hermeneutical lens; children of promise like Isaac; flesh persecutes Spirit; cast out slave woman; free not slave children. Additional notes on Jewish Isaac/Ishmael reception, textual variants (4:23, 25, 26, 28), and Gen 21:10 wording differences covered as apparatus.

**Not present / thin in range:** Extended treatment of 5:1+ beyond lead-in; full resolution of North/South Galatian geography beyond πρότερον; detailed Philo comparison beyond method contrast.
